topics.topic: The Sovereignty of God and Creation: God the creator and sustainer of the universe
learningObjectives: Analyze the two Biblical creation accounts in Genesis 1 and Genesis 2
Demonstrate God's supreme sovereignty over all created matter and physical laws
Explain humanity’s divine mandate as caretakers and stewards of the earthly environment

topics.topic: Leadership and Parental Responsibility: Eli and Samuel as case studies in moral guidance
learningObjectives: Contrast the priestly leadership of Eli and the corruption of his sons, Hophni and Phinehas
Evaluate the consequences of parental negligence in disciplining children (1 Samuel 2:12-25)
Examine the prophetic call and upright leadership of Samuel in Israel

topics.topic: The Covenant with God: Abraham and the covenant renewal at Shechem
learningObjectives: Trace the call of Abraham and God’s unconditional covenant promises (Genesis 12:1-9, 17:1-8)
Explain the sign of circumcision as the token of the Abrahamic covenant
Analyze Joshua’s challenge and the renewal of the covenant at Shechem (Joshua 24:1-28)

topics.topic: The Call to Repentance and Justice: Message of Prophet Amos and Hosea
learningObjectives: Analyze the social evils in Israel denounced by Amos: oppression of the poor, false weights, bribery
Explain Amos's declaration: 'Let justice roll down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream'
Explore Hosea's metaphor of unfaithfulness (Gomer) representing God's steadfast divine love (Hesed)

topics.topic: Faith and Works in Daily Life: Teachings of Apostle James (James 2:14-26)
learningObjectives: Explain the relationship between saving faith and active moral deeds according to James
Examine James’s argument that 'faith without works is dead'
Apply the principle of impartial treatment of the rich and poor in contemporary society

topics.topic: Dignity of Labor and Civil Obedience: Biblical ethics in governance (Romans 13)
learningObjectives: Explain Paul’s teaching on submission to civil governing authorities in Romans 13:1-7
Examine the Biblical view on paying taxes, tolls, and respecting law enforcement agencies
Highlight the Christian principle of hard work and honest trade (2 Thessalonians 3:6-12)

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Biblical Textual Exegesis Clinic
learningObjectives: Evaluate student mastery of Old Testament covenant theology and prophetic justice
Analyze selected biblical passages from Genesis, Amos, and Romans under exam conditions
Provide remedial instruction on drawing practical moral applications from Scripture

topics.topic: The Birth and Early Life of Jesus Christ: Prophecies, Annunciation, and Nativity
learningObjectives: Examine Isaiah’s prophecies of the Messiah (Isaiah 7:14, 9:6-7)
Compare the Annunciation accounts in Matthew 1 and Luke 1
Analyze the theological significance of the Incarnation and the visit of the Shepherds and Magi

topics.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus Christ: Moral lessons for Christian youth
learningObjectives: Describe the baptism of Jesus by John the Baptist in the Jordan River and divine confirmation
Analyze the three temptations in the wilderness (bread, temple pinnacle, kingdoms of the world)
Derive spiritual lessons on overcoming peer temptation through the word of God

topics.topic: The Ministry of Jesus: Beatitudes and the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5-7)
learningObjectives: Interpret the eight Beatitudes as kingdom values of meekness, mercy, and righteousness
Explain Christians as the salt of the earth and the light of the world
Analyze Christ's teachings on retaliation, love for enemies, and sincere prayer

topics.topic: Compassionate Miracles of Jesus: Healings, nature miracles, and feeding multitudes
learningObjectives: Categorize miracles of Jesus: healing miracles, nature miracles, and raising the dead
Examine the spiritual and humanitarian purpose behind Christ's miraculous interventions
Explain the role of faith in healing and receiving divine favor

topics.topic: Comprehensive CRS Revision & WAEC Question Paper Analysis
learningObjectives: Review key Old and New Testament themes covered during the first term
Practice constructing structured essays according to WAEC Paper 2 rubric specifications
Audit clarity of biblical citations and historical context in student essays

topics.topic: Terminal Examination, Script Moderation and Broadsheet Entry
learningObjectives: Administer standardized SSS 1 CRS examination covering biblical history and theology
Grade scripts accurately following official West African Examinations Council marking keys
Record and certify terminal marks for broadsheet entry
